mainTopic: A lost גט that was found, and the assumption that an absent husband is still alive
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: a lost גט found among the שליח's own things is valid even after a long time. Two אמוראים then give the הלכה on a found גט in their own words. One says it is valid if no one stopped there, and the other says only if no one passed there. They spelled out the rules instead of naming the תנאים because those names were sometimes swapped. The גמרא then explains the משנה's words חפיסה (a small leather flask) and דלוסקמא (an old man's pouch). A new משנה teaches that an absent person is assumed alive, so a גט is delivered, a כהן's wife eats תרומה, and a חטאת is offered. רבא tries to limit this to a man under eighty who is not a גוסס. A ברייתא about a hundred-year-old challenges him, and the גמרא suggests such a man may be a special case. אביי then raises contradictions from a גט that takes effect 'one hour before my death.' After several answers, אביי explains that the משנה follows רבי מאיר and the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and proves this from a case of wine bought from the כותים. רבא's own answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: Found among his own belongings: valid even after a long time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that defines 'right away' ends with a case that is always valid: the גט was found among the שליח's own things.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if he found it among his own belongings, then even after a long time it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא, quoted just before this, that explains what counts as finding a lost גט 'right away.' It adds a case where time does not matter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a lost גט is that the one he found might be a different גט, belonging to other people with the same names. If it turns up among his own belongings, no stranger's גט could have ended up there. So even after a long time, the גט is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: his belongings, his things
a long time
valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the time limit was simply dropped here. This is a special case: the place where the גט was found removes the doubt, so time no longer matters.

phrases.english: or that he found it among his belongings;
even after a long time, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא, begun on the previous page, that defines לאלתר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost גט found among the שליח's own belongings is valid no matter how much time has passed.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling: valid if no one stopped there
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה is that the found גט is valid as long as no person stopped at that spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, the הלכה is: as long as no person stopped there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא's ruling on which definition of 'right away' is the הלכה. According to שמואל, the test is whether anyone stayed at the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the more lenient view. A person who only walked past does not ruin the גט. Only someone who stopped and stayed there could have dropped another גט, so only that makes it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: it was said (introduces a statement of the אמוראים)
the practical law
stopped, stayed for a while

phrases.english: It was said: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
the halakha is: as long as no person stopped there.
phrases.notes: This matches the view of the יש אומרים, 'some say,' quoted in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling about the definitions in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The found גט is valid as long as no person stopped at that spot.

steps.title: A second ruling: valid only if no one passed there
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רב יצחק בר שמואל: the הלכה is that the גט is valid only if no person even passed by.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רב יצחק בר שמואל, the הלכה is: as long as no person passed there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second chain of אמוראים gives a different ruling. Here, even someone just walking by makes the found גט invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view is stricter than שמואל's. Even a person passing by might have dropped a גט. So the found גט is valid only if nobody at all went past.

keyTerms.meaning: passed by

steps.whyThisMatters: The two rulings differ only in one word, שהה versus עבר. But that word changes whether a passerby makes the גט invalid.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rav Yitzḥak bar Shmuel,
the halakha is: as long as no person passed there.
phrases.notes: This matches the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing ruling to שמואל's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The found גט is valid only if no person passed by that spot.

steps.title: Why not just name the תנא each one follows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why each אמורא repeated the actual rule instead of simply saying 'the הלכה follows this תנא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let this master say 'the הלכה follows that master,' and let the other master say 'the הלכה follows that master'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the two rulings were worded. Each rule already appears in the ברייתא under a תנא's name, so it seems simpler just to name him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal way to rule is to say 'הלכה כפלוני,' the הלכה follows So-and-so. Here both אמוראים spelled out the whole rule instead. The גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: let him say
master (a polite way to refer to a sage)
the הלכה follows that master

phrases.english: Let this master say, 'the halakha follows that master,'
phrases.notes: Here רב יהודה would say the הלכה follows the יש אומרים.

phrases.english: and let the other master say, 'the halakha follows that master'!
phrases.notes: And רבה בר בר חנה would say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מָר הֲלָכָה כְּמָר, וּמָר הֲלָכָה כְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way both rulings were phrased.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrasing of the rulings in steps 2 and 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each rule is already tied to a named תנא, so restating its content seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Because the names of the תנאים get switched
steps.stepSummary: The answer: some people swap which תנא said which view, so the אמוראים stated the rule itself to avoid a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there are those who reverse them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A name alone could be misread, but stating the rule itself cannot be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people had a different version of the ברייתא, with the opinions switched between the תנאים. If an אמורא only said 'הלכה כפלוני,' a listener might attach the wrong rule to that name. Saying the actual content prevents this.

keyTerms.meaning: they reverse, switch around

steps.whatToRemember: The two rulings are שלא שהה (no one stayed) and שלא עבר (no one passed). The אמוראים stated the rules themselves, because the names of the תנאים were sometimes switched.

phrases.english: Because there are those who reverse them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the names of the תנאים who hold each opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the wording was needed (to avoid confusion over names)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming the תנא would have been enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the names get swapped, only stating the content is safe.

steps.title: What is a חפיסה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a גט found in a חפיסה or a דלוסקמא, and asks what a חפיסה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He found it in a חפיסה or in a דלוסקמא': what is a חפיסה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for the meaning of an unclear word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a גט found in one of these containers can be valid. To understand the case, we first need to know what the container is.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of container (explained in the next step)
what is?

phrases.english: He found it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema:
What is a 'ḥafisa'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה for a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חפיסה

steps.title: A חפיסה is a small leather flask
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה explains that a חפיסה is a small leather flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: a small leather flask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a simple definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חמת is a container made of leather. A small one is called a חפיסה.

keyTerms.meaning: a leather flask or bottle
small

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
A small leather flask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חפיסה is a small leather flask.

steps.title: What is a דלוסקמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second word, דלוסקמא, means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a דלוסקמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the second container mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the question about חפיסה. Each container in the משנה gets explained.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of pouch (explained in the next step)

phrases.english: What is a 'deluskema'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דלוסקמא

steps.title: A דלוסקמא is an old man's pouch
steps.stepSummary: A דלוסקמא is the pouch that elderly people carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: An old man's pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the definition of דלוסקמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טליקא is a pouch or purse. A דלוסקמא is the kind that older men carry.

keyTerms.meaning: a pouch or purse
old men

steps.whatToRemember: חפיסה is a small leather flask, and דלוסקמא is an old man's pouch. These are the two containers named in the משנה.

phrases.english: A pouch of old men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דלוסקמא is an old man's pouch.

steps.title: The משנה: we assume an absent person is still alive
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules in three cases that we assume an absent person is still alive: a husband who sent a גט, a כהן who went overseas, and a person who sent his חטאת from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an agent brings a גט and the husband was old or sick when the agent left him, the agent still gives the גט to the woman, because we assume the husband is alive. An ordinary Jewish woman married to a כהן whose husband went overseas may keep eating תרומה, because we assume he is alive. If a person sends his חטאת from overseas, the כהנים offer it, because we assume he is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches one rule, that we assume a person is still alive, and shows it in three different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט only works if the husband is alive when it is given, since a dead man cannot divorce. A non-כהן woman eats תרומה only because of her living כהן husband. A חטאת whose owner has died cannot be offered. In all three cases the משנה says not to worry: we assume the person is still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Based on the assumption that he is still alive
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים; members of a כהן's household may eat it
Literally 'a land across the sea'; any faraway place
A sin-offering brought to atone for an accidental sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This assumption lets people act normally on behalf of someone who is far away, without proof that he is still alive. The rest of the סוגיא asks how far it stretches.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who brings a bill of divorce,
and when he left him, he was old or sick –
gives it to her on the assumption that he is alive.
An Israelite woman married to a priest,
and her husband went to a country overseas –
eats teruma on the assumption that he is alive.
One who sends his sin-offering from a country overseas –
they offer it on the assumption that he is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט, וְהִנִּיחוֹ זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of the חפיסה and דלוסקמא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An absent person is assumed to be alive. So a גט may be delivered, a כהן's wife may eat תרומה, and a חטאת may be offered.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to an old man under eighty and an ordinary sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the assumption applies only to an old man who has not reached eighty and to an ordinary sick person. It does not apply to a man over eighty or to a גוסס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the משנה only meant an old man who has not yet reached eighty, and an ordinary sick person, since most sick people live. But an old man who has reached eighty, or a גוסס, is not assumed alive, since most people who are גוססים die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבא narrowing the משנה's rule. He says it does not cover every old or sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא bases the rule on what usually happens. Most sick people recover, so we can assume the husband is alive. Most people who are גוססים die, so that assumption no longer holds. He also places a very old man, past eighty, outside the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught it about...'; a phrase that narrows a rule
Literally 'years of strength'; the age of eighty
A person in his last moments before death
The majority; what usually happens

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חולה and גוסס. A חולה is an ordinary sick person, and most recover. A גוסס is actively dying, and most die.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rava said:
They taught this only about an old man
who has not reached 'strength';
and a sick person, since most sick people live;
but an old man who has reached 'strength',
and a dying person, since most dying people go on to die;
no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא זָקֵן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לִגְבוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the 'old or sick' cases of the משנה in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The assumption that he is alive applies to an old man under eighty and to an ordinary sick person. It does not apply to a man over eighty or to a גוסס.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from a ברייתא about a hundred-year-old man
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: even if the husband was a hundred years old, the agent gives the גט on the assumption that he is alive. This contradicts רבא's age limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: a ברייתא teaches that if an agent brings a גט and left the husband old, even a hundred years old, he gives it to her on the assumption that the husband is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's limit using a ברייתא that clearly covers a man far past eighty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a man who has reached eighty is not assumed alive. The ברייתא says even a hundred-year-old is assumed alive. These cannot both be true. The challenge speaks only about old age, not about the גוסס.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him, using a תנאי source
אביי, the אמורא who often debates with רבא
One hundred years old

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
One who brings a bill of divorce and left him old –
even one hundred years old,
gives it to her on the assumption that he is alive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's limit from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an old man who has reached eighty is not assumed alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly assumes that even a hundred-year-old is alive. That directly contradicts an age-eighty cutoff.

steps.title: רבא's statement is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes with 'תיובתא': רבא's statement is refuted by the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its verdict. אביי's challenge stands, and רבא's statement is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot argue with a clear ברייתא, so the גמרא first declares רבא's age-eighty limit refuted. The ברייתא's ruling stands: even a hundred-year-old is assumed alive. The next step offers a possible defense of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A final refutation; the view that was challenged is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says an absent husband is assumed alive. רבא tried to exclude a man past eighty, and the ברייתא about a hundred-year-old seems to refute him. Step 14 offers a way to save רבא's limit for an ordinary old man.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 12 by accepting it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא about a hundred-year-old seems to refute רבא's age-eighty limit, though step 14 offers a way to defend it.

steps.title: Someone who reached a hundred has proven he is exceptional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to defend רבא. A man who has already lived far past normal age is treated as a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: once he has gone far beyond normal age, he has gone far beyond, so we treat him as someone who keeps living.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after calling רבא 'refuted,' the גמרא offers a possible defense. The hundred-year-old in the ברייתא is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's eighty-year limit is about an ordinary old man, who might die at any time. A man who has reached a hundred has already shown that his body breaks the normal pattern. So we assume he will keep living, and the ברייתא does not really contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another possible answer)
He went far beyond (the normal lifespan)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the defense means רבא's rule is thrown out. The eighty-year limit still holds for a normal old man. Only someone who has already reached an extreme age is treated as an exception.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since he went far beyond, he went far beyond.
phrases.notes: He means: a man who made it to a hundred has shown he is unusual, so we expect him to keep going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a defense of רבא after the תיובתא in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: an exceptional lifespan versus an ordinary old man
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about a hundred-year-old disproves רבא's eighty-year limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man who has already reached an extreme age is a special case. רבא's limit applies only to ordinary old men.

steps.title: The גט case assumes life, but the תרומה case worries about death
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows רבה a contradiction. The משנה assumes an old or sick husband is alive, while a ברייתא worries that a husband might die at any moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised a contradiction to רבה. We learned: if the agent bringing a גט left the husband old or sick, he gives it to her on the assumption that the husband is alive. But a ברייתא says: if a husband said 'This is your גט, one hour before my death,' she is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets two sources side by side that seem to disagree about whether we assume a person stays alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, we trust that the husband is still alive, so the גט can be given. In the ברייתא, the wife of a כהן must stop eating תרומה right away. The reason is that the husband might die in an hour, and then the גט would already have taken effect an hour earlier. That ruling treats death as possible at any moment, which clashes with the משנה's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)
And contrast it with (introduces the clashing source)
On the assumption that he is alive
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which his household may eat

phrases.english: Abaye raised a contradiction to Rabba:
We learned: one who brings a bill of divorce
and left him old or sick
gives it to her on the assumption that he is alive.
And contrast it with this:
"This is your bill of divorce"
one hour before his death
she is forbidden to eat teruma immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new contradiction about the assumption of life in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that we assume an old or sick husband is still alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא worries that a husband might die at any moment, which does not fit the משנה's assumption that he stays alive.

steps.title: With תרומה you can be strict, but with a גט you cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that you cannot compare תרומה to גיטין. Being strict about תרומה is easy, but being strict about a גט would make sending one impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you setting תרומה against גיטין? With תרומה, being careful is possible. With a גט, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the two rulings do not truly clash. They involve different kinds of laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, the wife can simply eat ordinary food and lose nothing important, so we may worry even about a far-off chance of death. If we worried that the husband might have died every time a גט is sent, no one could ever send a גט through an agent. That is why the גט case relies on the assumption that he is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Possible
Not possible
Bills of divorce

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that how strict we are about a doubt can depend on whether being strict is even workable in practice.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Are you setting teruma against bills of divorce?!
With teruma it is possible,
phrases.notes: She can just eat regular food instead, so being careful costs little.

phrases.english: with a bill of divorce it is not possible.
phrases.notes: If we always worried that the husband had died, a גט could never be sent with an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's contradiction from step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two areas of law (תרומה versus גיטין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings are about the same question, whether a person might have died, so they should match.
steps.terutzMaskana: With תרומה we can afford to be strict. With a גט, being strict is unworkable, so we rely on the assumption that he is alive.

steps.title: Setting up a contradiction between two תרומה rulings
steps.stepSummary: Since רבה split תרומה from גיטין, the גמרא now sets one תרומה ruling against another. It first quotes the משנה's ruling that a כהן's wife keeps eating תרומה when her husband is overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he set תרומה against תרומה. We learned: a בת ישראל married to a כהן, whose husband went overseas, eats תרומה on the assumption that he is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new contradiction. It quotes the first side, the משנה's תרומה ruling, and the clashing ברייתא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer depended on תרומה being an area where we are strict. But this משנה lets the wife keep eating תרומה, trusting that her absent husband is alive. That seems to clash with the 'one hour before my death' ruling, where she must stop right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not from a כהן family
Who is married to a כהן
A land overseas, far away

phrases.english: And he set teruma against teruma:
We learned: an Israelite woman married to a priest,
and her husband went overseas
eats teruma on the assumption that he is alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה's answer in step 16 by finding a clash within תרומה itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the two תרומה rulings: the משנה's (she eats, assuming he is alive) and the ברייתא's ('one hour before my death', she stops at once)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a כהן's wife eat תרומה, trusting that her absent husband is alive. So why should the ברייתא make her stop out of fear that he will die?

steps.title: A ruling about a deathbed divorce contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if a husband gives a גט that takes effect 'one hour before my death,' his wife may not eat תרומה from that moment on. This clashes with the משנה, which assumes a distant husband is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: if a husband says, 'This is your גט, taking effect one hour before my death,' she is forbidden to eat תרומה right away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the contradiction it set up in step 17. Here it quotes the ברייתא that clashes with the משנה about the כהן's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, we fear the husband could die within the next hour. If he did, the גט would already have taken effect, so she is forbidden to eat תרומה right now. The משנה, however, does not fear that a distant husband has died, so his wife keeps eating תרומה. These are two rulings about תרומה with two opposite attitudes toward sudden death.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other. This word introduces a contradiction between two sources.
One hour before his death
Immediately, from right now

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, רבה defended the משנה by saying that תרומה and גיטין work differently. This contradiction is harder, because both rulings are about תרומה. That answer can no longer help.

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction: "This is your bill of divorce"
one hour before my death,
she is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup of step 17 by bringing the opposing ruling about תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a כהן's wife keeps eating תרומה when her husband is overseas
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ruling about תרומה worries about the husband's sudden death, and the other does not. Both cannot be right.

steps.title: In the divorce case, she is sure to become forbidden someday
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק says the ברייתא is different. There the husband has definitely forbidden her to himself from one hour before his death, so we treat the doubt as starting now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא, son of רב יצחק, said: It is different there, because he made her forbidden to himself starting one hour before his death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא tries to answer the contradiction by showing how the two cases differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, nothing ever has to happen that would forbid the wife. In the ברייתא, the גט is set up so that she will surely become forbidden one day, because everyone dies. Since her becoming forbidden is certain, we already worry about it now.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
He made her forbidden to himself

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Adda, son of Rav Yitzchak, said:
It is different there,
for he made her forbidden to himself
one hour before his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 18 by showing the cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings deal with the same worry about sudden death, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the ברייתא, the husband made it certain that she will become forbidden, so the worry already applies now. In the משנה, there is no such certainty.

steps.title: Maybe she dies first
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects רב אדא's answer. It is not certain the גט will ever take effect, because the wife might die before the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: How do we know he will die first? Maybe she will die first!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down רב אדא's answer from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's answer depended on the claim that the wife will surely become forbidden one day. רב פפא points out that if she dies first, the גט never takes effect at all. So her becoming forbidden is not certain, and the ברייתא again looks like the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
First
Perhaps

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenged it:
From where do we know that he will die first?
Perhaps she will die first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רב אדא's distinction
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is not certain that she will become forbidden, because she might die before her husband and the גט would never take effect.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about worrying over death
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the two sources follow different opinions. The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who does not worry about sudden death. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: There is no difficulty. This source follows רבי מאיר, who does not worry about death. That source follows רבי יהודה, who does worry about death.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב אדא's answer failed, אביי gives a new answer. He says the two rulings come from two תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not try to make the two cases different. He accepts that the rulings really do conflict, and he explains that they follow different opinions. The משנה, which lets the wife keep eating, is רבי מאיר. The ברייתא, which forbids her right away, is רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
He is concerned about death
A תנא; here, the one who does not worry about sudden death
A תנא; here, the one who does worry about sudden death

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (the wife keeps eating תרומה) follows רבי מאיר, who does not worry about death. The ברייתא (she is forbidden right away) follows רבי יהודה, who does.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר – דְּלָא חָיֵישׁ לְמִיתָה,
phrases.english: This one follows Rabbi Meir, who is not concerned about death,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה that lets the wife keep eating תרומה.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Yehuda, who is concerned about death.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא about the גט that takes effect one hour before death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 rejected the first answer, אביי offers a different answer to the contradiction of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings come from one view and must somehow fit together.
steps.terutzMaskana: They come from רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who disagree about whether to worry over sudden death.

steps.title: רבי מאיר lets a person drink now and separate later
steps.stepSummary: To show that רבי מאיר does not worry about something happening suddenly, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A buyer of untithed wine from the כותים names the portions he will separate later, and רבי מאיר lets him drink right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who buys wine from the כותים says: 'Two לוגין that I will separate in the future are תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני and drinks right away. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the source for אביי's claim. It quotes רבי מאיר's ruling about wine bought from the כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine still has to be separated, but רבי מאיר lets the buyer drink now and rely on a separation he will make later. He does not worry that something might happen before he gets to it. This matches the idea that רבי מאיר does not worry about sudden death.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, who are assumed not to have separated תרומה and מעשרות
Plural of לוֹג, a liquid measure
First tithe, given to a לוי
Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
He redeems it, moving its holiness onto money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the buyer is separating the wine now. He only names the amounts. The actual separating happens later, yet רבי מאיר lets him drink already.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who buys wine from among the Samaritans,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ
phrases.english: says: Two log that I will separate in the future
are hereby תרומה;
ten are first tithe;
nine are second tithe;

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵיחֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה מִיָּד – דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and he redeems it and drinks immediately; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: He's redeeming the מעשר שני wine, moving its holiness onto money so he can drink the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing the source behind אביי's claim in step 21 about רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר does not worry about sudden death
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about wine bought from the כותים, where רבי מאיר lets the buyer drink now and separate later

steps.title: Three Sages forbid drinking the wine right away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbidding what רבי מאיר allowed. This shows that רבי יהודה worries about a sudden mishap, so the proof for אביי's split is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא about the wine. Three Sages disagree with רבי מאיר and do not let the buyer drink before he actually separates the portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These Sages worry that the wineskin might burst before he separates תרומה and מעשר, which would mean he drank טבל. רבי מאיר does not worry about that. This matches אביי's claim from step 21: רבי מאיר does not worry about sudden events like death, but רבי יהודה does.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbid it
The תנא who worries about sudden events. According to אביי, the ברייתא about the גט follows his view.
A תנא who agrees with רבי יהודה here
Another תנא who agrees with רבי יהודה here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר is not worried about sudden events, so the husband is presumed alive and the wine may be drunk right away. רבי יהודה is worried about sudden events, so the wife may not eat תרומה and the wine may not be drunk yet. This is how אביי explains the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The wine case has nothing to do with death or divorce. It is brought only to show the general attitude of each תנא toward unexpected events, and the גמרא then applies that attitude to the husband's possible sudden death.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 22 by giving the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי יהודה worries about sudden events and רבי מאיר does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא about wine bought from the כותים, where רבי יהודה and his colleagues forbid drinking it right away

steps.title: רבא begins his own answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רבא, who is about to give a different way of resolving the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא about the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces רבא. It sets up his statement, which comes right after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After אביי's answer that the two sources follow different תנאים, רבא steps in with another approach. What he actually says has not been quoted yet, so for now we only know that a new answer is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often discusses סוגיות together with אביי
Said. This word opens a new statement.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's resolution has been proven, the גמרא introduces רבא's separate approach to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The contradiction from step 18 might be settled only by אביי's split between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא will offer another way to settle it. His words are not quoted yet.
